resources.string: This thin coat of dense connective tissue covers the outer surface of the renal cortex.
The rounded corpuscle contains a tuft of capillaries, the glomerulus, within Bowman\'s capsule. Corpuscles lie in the cortical labyrinth, not in the straight rays.
Despite its name, this bundle lies in the cortex. Straight segments of nephron tubules and collecting ducts run together here toward or away from the medulla.
The tissue between the straight rays contains coiled proximal and distal tubules, with rounded renal corpuscles scattered among them.
The broad end of the medullary pyramid meets the cortex. The pyramid narrows inward toward its papilla.
This inward extension of cortical tissue lies between adjacent medullary pyramids.
Collecting ducts run lengthwise and join into larger ducts deeper in the pyramid. The terminal ducts open at the papillary tip.
The rounded tip of the pyramid projects into a minor calyx, a cup that receives urine from the openings of the papillary ducts.
Calyces and renal pelvis in section
This cup surrounds the projecting tip of a renal papilla. Its narrow neck opens into a larger calyx.
The two smaller cups shown above join into this wider branch, which opens into the renal pelvis.
Major calyces join in this broad cavity. It narrows at the kidney hilum to continue as the ureter.
